questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A $20,000 auto loan at 6% APR for 60 months has a payment of $386.66. How much interest is paid over the loan?
questions.intro: An auto loan is an installment loan. Total paid = monthly payment × number of months. Interest = total paid − amount borrowed.

misconceptions.C: Uses 6% for 5 years as simple interest on the full amount
misconceptions.D: Gives the total paid instead of the interest

sources: CFPB (Auto loans): Getting preapproved and comparing the total cost of loans helps borrowers; dealers may arrange financing and can add to the rate a lender offers. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/auto-loans/)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A $20,000 loan at 6% for 72 months has a $331.46 payment and $3,865.12 of interest. The 60-month loan has $3,199.60 of interest. How much more interest does the longer loan cost?
questions.intro: A longer term lowers the payment but usually raises the total interest, because the balance is paid down more slowly.

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Why should Maya get preapproved by a bank or credit union before visiting a dealer?

choices.text: Because dealers are not allowed to offer any financing at all
Because a preapproval guarantees the lowest price on the car
Because preapproval removes the need for a credit check later
To have a rate to compare

questions.correct_answer: To have a rate to compare
questions.intro: Dealers can arrange financing by sending your application to lenders, and may add to the rate a lender approves. A preapproval from your own bank or credit union gives you an offer to compare against.
questions.feedback: A preapproval is a benchmark: take the dealer's offer only if it beats it.
sources: CFPB (Auto loans): Getting preapproved and comparing the total cost of loans helps borrowers; dealers may arrange financing and can add to the rate a lender offers. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/auto-loans/)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Why can an 84-month loan with a small down payment be risky?

choices.text: Long loans always have lower total interest than short ones
The loan can exceed the car's value
Lenders cannot repossess cars on loans longer than five years
Payments rise every year on a long fixed-rate auto loan

questions.correct_answer: The loan can exceed the car's value
questions.intro: Cars lose value quickly. On a long loan with little down, the balance falls more slowly than the car's value, so the borrower can be "underwater" for years.
questions.feedback: Slow payoff plus fast depreciation can leave the borrower owing more than the car is worth.
sources: CFPB (Auto loans): Getting preapproved and comparing the total cost of loans helps borrowers; dealers may arrange financing and can add to the rate a lender offers. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/auto-loans/)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Two loans have the same amount and term. Which costs less in interest?

choices.text: The one with the lower APR
The one with the higher APR, since it pays off faster
They cost the same because the amount is the same
The one from the dealer that is closest to home

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Offer 1: 0% APR for 60 months on a $30,000 car. Offer 2: a $3,000 rebate, then $27,000 at 5% for 60 months ($509.52 a month). Which costs less in total?

choices.text: Offer 2, by $571.20
Offer 2, by $3,000
Offer 1, by $571.20
Offer 1, by $3,000

questions.intro: Dealers sometimes offer a choice: a low rate or a cash rebate. Compare the total paid under each.

misconceptions.B: Counts the rebate but not the interest
misconceptions.D: Ignores the interest paid on Offer 2

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: On a simple-interest auto loan with no prepayment penalty, what does an extra $100 payment toward principal do?

choices.text: Nothing, because interest is fixed when the loan starts
Reduces the interest charged later
Raises the next monthly payment by $100
Adds a $100 fee to the loan balance

questions.intro: Most auto loans charge interest on the remaining balance. Paying extra principal shrinks the balance, so later interest is smaller. Check the contract for a prepayment penalty.
questions.feedback: A lower balance means less interest from then on.

misconceptions.A: Believes interest is set in advance
misconceptions.D: Confuses a payment with a fee

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Alex cosigns a friend's car loan. If the friend stops paying, what happens?

choices.text: Only the friend's credit is affected by any missed payment
The lender must forgive the loan because there are two signers
The car is transferred to Alex for free
Alex must pay

questions.intro: A cosigner promises to repay if the borrower does not. Missed payments appear on the cosigner's credit report too.
questions.feedback: A cosigner is fully responsible for the debt.

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A car is totaled. Insurance pays its value, $14,000, but the loan balance is $18,000. How much would GAP coverage pay?
questions.intro: GAP (guaranteed asset protection) covers the gap between the car's value and the loan balance if the car is totaled or stolen. It is optional and often cheaper from an insurer than a dealer.

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Jo expects to miss a car payment next month. What is the best first step?

choices.text: Hide the car so the lender cannot find it
Ignore the lender's letters until the problem passes
Call the lender before the payment is missed
Take a payday loan at very high cost

questions.correct_answer: Call the lender before the payment is missed
questions.intro: Lenders may offer a deferral or modified plan if contacted early.
questions.feedback: Early contact gives the most options.

misconceptions.A: Can add costs and legal trouble
misconceptions.D: Trades one problem for a costlier one
